_meta.indication: Indicated in adults for the treatment of acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused by susceptible isolates of designated Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study RX-3341-302 (Study 302), IV delafloxacin vs IV vancomycin plus aztreonam in ABSSSI
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind trial comparing IV delafloxacin to IV vancomycin plus aztreonam
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI); patients randomized 1:1 to delafloxacin 300 mg IV q12h or vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h plus aztreonam 2 g q12h
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response of >=20% reduction in lesion erythema compared with baseline at 48 to 72 hours after initiation of therapy, with no evidence of clinical failure; prespecified noninferiority margin of -10%
pivotal_trials.n: 660 patients randomized (331 to IV delafloxacin, 329 to vancomycin plus aztreonam)
pivotal_trials.result: Objective clinical response 259/331 (78.2%) delafloxacin vs 266/329 (80.9%) vancomycin plus aztreonam; treatment difference -2.6 (95% CI -8.8, 3.6), demonstrating noninferiority

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study RX-3341-303 (Study 303), IV-to-oral delafloxacin vs IV vancomycin plus aztreonam in ABSSSI
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind trial of IV/oral delafloxacin (mandatory oral switch) vs IV vancomycin plus aztreonam
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with ABSSSI; delafloxacin IV every 12 hours for six doses followed by delafloxacin 450 mg orally every 12 hours, vs vancomycin plus aztreonam
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response of >=20% reduction in lesion erythema compared with baseline at 48 to 72 hours after initiation of therapy, with no evidence of clinical failure; prespecified noninferiority margin of -10%
pivotal_trials.n: 850 patients randomized (423 to IV/oral delafloxacin, 427 to vancomycin plus aztreonam)
pivotal_trials.result: Objective clinical response 354/423 (83.7%) delafloxacin vs 344/427 (80.6%) vancomycin plus aztreonam; treatment difference 3.1 (95% CI -2.0, 8.3), demonstrating noninferiority

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=2%): nausea (8%), diarrhea (8%), headache (3%), transaminase elevations (3%), and vomiting (2%). Serious class risks include tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects, exacerbation of myasthenia gravis, hypersensitivity reactions, and C. difficile-associated diarrhea
target_moa: Delafloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibacterial; its activity is due to inhibition of both bacterial topoisomerase IV and DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II), enzymes required for bacterial DNA replication, transcription, repair, and recombination

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for serious adverse reactions including tendinitis, tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, central nervous system effects, and exacerbation of myasthenia gravis; discontinue and avoid fluoroquinolones in patients who experience any of these

advisory_committee.vote: The NDAs were not discussed at an advisory committee meeting as there were no specific issues that required input from the committee

summary.text: Delafloxacin (Baxdela) received QIDP designation for the ABSSSI indication on September 8, 2012, and fast track designation on December 18, 2012; based on the QIDP designation both NDAs received a priority review. Efficacy was based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 noninferiority trials, and the applications were approved as full (not accelerated) approvals.

requirement.text: 3220-2: Conduct a tissue distribution study in pregnant rats treated during organogenesis with the oral and IV formulations (with SBECD/Captisol) to assess distribution to the reproductive tract and developing fetus

citations.quote: **3220-2:** Conduct a tissue distribution study in pregnant rats treated during the period of organogenesis with the oral formulation and with the intravenous formulation of Baxdela with the excipient sulfobutylether beta-cyclodextrin (SBECD) to assess the distribution of the drug substance to the reproductive tract and developing fetus.

citations.quote: **3220-3:** If the results of the tissue distribution studies from PMR 3220-2 demonstrate greater exposure of the fetus / maternal reproductive tract to delafloxacin with the intravenous formulation, conduct an embryo-fetal developmental toxicology study in pregnant rats treated during the period of organogenesis with the intravenous formulation of Baxdela to identify possible effects of delafloxa
